question: Should OpenClaw adopt this private final-capture operation and its durable recovery-record contract before the RFC ownership split, aggregate recovery-point prerequisite, and host lifecycle integration have been accepted?
rationale: The patch is a new core persistence and lifecycle boundary, not a repair to an established behavior; code review cannot determine whether this is the intended permanent owner split or whether it belongs with a future host adapter.

options.title: Accept the staged core contract
options.body: Approve the private capture boundary after the owners accept the RFC and prerequisite recovery-point inventory contract, then require rebasing and real command proof before merge.

options.title: Keep capture with the future host integration
options.body: Defer this hidden command until the host adapter, closure evidence, and durable acceptance responsibilities can be reviewed as one cohesive boundary.

options.title: Narrow the proposal further
options.body: Retain only a reviewed generic snapshot seam and move handoff-specific intent, replay, and quarantine semantics out of core until their permanent owner is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept the staged core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the private capture boundary after the owners accept the RFC and prerequisite recovery-point inventory contract, then require rebasing and real command proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed participant across the linked recovery-point stack and can clarify the proposal, while an OpenClaw owner must make the final product decision.
